text:
Priya Nair: Quick heads up — planning a Console/UI deploy today at 14:00 UTC (v3.4.1). Need smoke owner + rollback ready. Will do a 10% canary for 10m then ramp. CDN invalidation + edge warmup after canary. Who can own smoke?

Jordan Kim: I can own smoke checks. I’ll be on call 13:45–15:00 UTC. What exact checks do you want? :thumbsup:

Priya Nair: Awesome — thanks Jordan. Short smoke checklist (what I want validated during canary):
- login / auth flows
- create basic project + upload small file
- open Dashboard and Model settings (assets load)
- run a short text-gen request end-to-end
- confirm no 5xx on main Console routes

Also: after canary success we’ll invalidate CDN paths `/static/*` and `/assets/*` and run edge priming for the top bundles.

Carlos Mendes: I’ll handle edge warmup and the invalidation. Plan: run CloudFront invalidation once canary at 10% looks good, then kick a three-region curl warmup to prime edges. CloudFront distro id: `E1Z3A4BCDEFG` (confirmed).

Sam Lee: Rollback readiness: previous build `v3.4.0` will be tagged and kept on hot storage. I can perform a rollback; my window is free from 13:30–15:30 UTC. Criteria: if canary error rate >5% or key flows failing, we rollback.

Jordan Kim: For the smoke I'll run this quick checklist in order and post results here:
- login ✓
- create project ✓
- open dataset page ✓
- run small inference (sanity) ✓
- check browser console for missing assets / 404s ✓
- check Sentry/Logs for 5xx spikes ✓
(Will post timestamps + any errors)

Priya Nair: Nice. Two operational notes:
1) Set asset Cache-Control to short TTL (60s) during rollout so invalidation is quick, then switch to long cache after stable.
2) Keep previous asset manifest handy in `s3://redwood-console-assets/manifests/` and tags in the deploy service for fast rollback.

Carlos Mendes: Invalidation + warmup commands I’ll run (posting here so infra knows):
```bash
# CloudFront invalidation
aws cloudfront create-invalidation --distribution-id E1Z3A4BCDEFG --paths "/static/*" "/assets/*"

# Quick region warmups (example)
curl -s -H 'Host: console.redwood.ai' https://console.redwood.ai/static/js/main.bundle.js > /dev/null
curl -s -H 'Host: console.redwood.ai' https://console.redwood.ai/assets/vendor.css > /dev/null
```
I’ll run these from us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1 after invalidation. Will post success/fail counts.

deploy-bot: Ticket created: DL-4821 — UI deploy v3.4.1 (canary 10% for 10m -> 100% in 30m). Link: https://deployments.redwood.ai/DL-4821 :robot_face:

Jordan Kim: Quick note on metrics I’ll watch during canary: 1) 5xx rate on /console/*, 2) TTFB for main bundle, 3) Sentry errors grouped by release, 4) JS asset 404s. If any of those spike I’ll call rollback.

Sam Lee: Rollback command (for ops reference):
`deploy-bot rollback ui v3.4.0 --force`
I’ll only run after we confirm smoke fails or infra flags an outage.

Priya Nair: Perfect — small housekeeping: leave feature flags as-is for this canary, don't change auth or oauth configs during the window. Also post any canary failures as replies here with screenshots/logs.

Carlos Mendes: Setting Cache-Control on edge to `max-age=60` now for files in the deploy path; will switch to `max-age=86400` after 1h stable. Invalidations queued to run after Jordan signs off on canary.

Jordan Kim: On it. I’ll run smoke at 14:10 UTC once canary rolls. Will post a short pass/fail and any errors. :rocket:

Priya Nair: Thanks team — ping me in this thread for anything urgent during the window. I’ll coordinate canary ramp and final cutoff. :white_check_mark:
